title: docs(spec): state what the map renderer actually does with an undeclared key in `map`
body:
Fixes #18910

Clause-②: no — docblock prose only. The accept set, the key list and `strictObject` are byte-identical; no public surface moves.

## What the card said, and what I measured

The card said `ListMapConfigSchema`'s docblock asserts a mechanism the renderer does not perform:

> it validates `schema.map` against a local zod schema with exactly these keys, so an extra key here would be dropped there

I re-derived every reading first-hand at the pin — `.objectui-sha` reads `53ded82bf7a494f54e344e19099dbf00854b8694`, and I checked that commit out into its own detached worktree (`git worktree add --detach`, HEAD `53ded82bf7a494f54e344e19099dbf00854b8694`), never objectui `main`. Rather than reading the source and believing it, I extracted the pinned declarations byte-exact by line range (anchor-verified, sha256-stamped) and **executed** them under zod 4.4.3 — the version the pin's own lockfile resolves. Every zero/negative reading below carries a same-subject control that HITS.

| # | reading at the pin | lit control | control result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ObjectMapConfigSchema` (`packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts:562`) is a plain `z.object`: `safeParse({…, extraKey})` → `success=true`, **zero issues**, no warning | (a) the same extracted declaration with `.strict()` appended, same input; (b) the real declaration with `zoom: 'far'` | (a) `success=false` → `unrecognized_keys` at the ROOT path; (b) `success=false` → `invalid_type@zoom`. The probe can see closure, and it reaches the schema |
| 2 | `getMapConfig` (`packages/plugin-map/src/ObjectMap.tsx:373-376`) consults that `safeParse` only to pick a `console.warn`: with an undeclared key, **0 warn calls** | same call with `zoom: 'far'` | exactly **1** warn, `[ObjectMap] Invalid map configuration:` — the warn path is reachable and my capture works |
| 3 | `:378` returns a spread of the AUTHORED block: `getMapConfig({map:{locationField,extraKey}})` → `{"locationField":"loc","extraKey":"x"}` — carried through | the failing-parse call above still returns `{"locationField":"loc","zoom":"far"}` | the parse result is provably not the value |
| 4 | **New.** On the path this block actually takes, the key IS dropped: `resolveListMapConfig` (`packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx:113`) → `{"locationField":"loc","titleField":"name"}` — `extraKey` gone, and `style` with it | the declared `locationField` / `titleField` in the same call | both survive — the instrument transmits, so the two absences are readings |

Per the dispatcher's warning about counting rather than printing: every negative above is a printed value, not a count. The one search-shaped reading — "`objectql.zod.ts` declares nothing strict" — is printed too: its only `strict` hit in that file is a **comment** at `:392` (「Note `UserActionsConfigSchema` is NOT `.strict()`」), and the lit control that the search would find a real one is `packages/types/src/zod/complex.zod.ts:635` → `}).strict();`.

## What turned out false — in the card, not in the fix

The card's three readings are all accurate, and its line numbers still land. But its conclusion — *"an undeclared key inside `map` is neither flagged nor dropped by the renderer"* — **is false for the path this block governs.** A spec list view's `map` block never reaches `getMapConfig` as a `map` block: `ListView` and `ObjectView` flatten it through the hand-listed `FLAT_MAP_CONFIG_KEYS` whitelist first, and both emit flat props ("neither flattener emits a `map` key at all"). So the docblock's *outcome* word — "would be dropped" — happens to hold; its *mechanism* — a closed local zod schema — does not, anywhere.

That distinction is the whole fix, because the mechanism is what a future editor would act on. Believing "the renderer validates it" and relaxing this block to `passthrough` buys an author no check at all: the key dies in a whitelist without a word, and the one schema that could have reported it is open and warn-only.

## The edit

Before:

> Closed (strict) from the start: the map renderer's read set is itself closed — it validates `schema.map` against a local zod schema with exactly these keys, so an extra key here would be dropped there.

After (opening sentence; the full replacement is in the diff):

> Closed (strict) from the start, and the strictness stands on its own: it does NOT rest on the renderer refusing an undeclared key, because nothing downstream refuses one.

followed by the two measured bullets, and by the reason the strictness survives losing its old argument: nothing downstream reports an undeclared key, so **this parse is the only place an author is told anywhere** — `map` is not in objectui's `LIST_VIEW_LOCAL_OVERRIDES`, so objectui's own `ListViewSchema` imports this block by reference and the document check on that side is this same schema.

⛔ `strictObject` is untouched. No key was added, removed or renamed.

## The anchors are now machine-checked, not just asserted

This defect is a cross-repo claim that rotted because nothing re-read it. `check:objectui-pin-citations` already has the instrument for that — an anchor that quotes its first line is verified against objectui at the pin — and it was sitting at zero coverage. The seven anchors in this record now carry their quoted line, so the gate reds on the next pin bump instead of rotting, and `ASSERTED_ANCHOR_FLOOR` moves `0 → 7` with its note rewritten (that ratchet is an equality in both directions).

Verified, not assumed: `check:objectui-pin-citations` prints `7 anchor content assertion(s) verified against objectui at 53ded82bf`.

**Ablation — the new assertions can fail.** Committed the change first, then mutated one quoted line through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (on-disk anchor hit + blob hashes, not an editor's exit code): `export const ObjectMapConfigSchema = z.object({` → `… z.strictObject({`. The gate went **exit 1** and named it:

```
✗ packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts:1764 — the asserted first line does not match
  `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts:562` at this pin.
      asserted: export const ObjectMapConfigSchema = z.strictObject({
      actually: export const ObjectMapConfigSchema = z.object({
```

Restore was verified on disk, not by an exit code: `blob after restore 358aed5fc71d99c6…` == `blob at HEAD 358aed5fc71d99c6…`, `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Tests and gates

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/ui/view.test.ts src/ui/component.test.ts src/ui/view-gantt-tree-config-closed-15469.test.ts src/ui/view-strictness-batch18.test.ts` — **4 files, 878 tests passed**.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` — green (includes `check:scripts-typecheck`, which covers the edited gate script, and `check:test-typecheck`).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build && … check:generated` — **all 16 generated artifacts up to date**; no regeneration was owed.
- Gate families derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (its own change-set derivation, not a hand-written list) and run; six dist-reading gates first refused with `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` against a `dist` older than the edit, and were green on re-run after `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` — recorded as NOT MEASURED → measured, never as findings.

## Acceptance notes

Noted here rather than filed or fixed — ⛔ no diff was widened for any of them.

1. **`ListMapConfigSchema.style` does not reach the renderer on the list-view path at this pin.** `#18406` added `style` because `getMapConfig` reads `schema.map?.style`. Measured: `FLAT_MAP_CONFIG_KEYS` is this block's keys **minus `style`**, `resolveListMapConfig` drops it (printed above), `baseProps` carries no `style`/`mapStyle`, and `mapStyle` appears in neither flattener (printed hits; lit control: `locationField`, which IS forwarded, hits in both files). Radius of the instrument: the two flatten sites plus `baseProps` in `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` and `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` at `53ded82b` — it does not cover an `object-map` component node written by hand, where `map.style` does reach `getMapConfig`. A style URL authored through this face parses green and the map renders on the default demo tiles, silently. The landing repo would be objectui, and the docblock sentence it touches is `#18406`'s ruling text, so it is a card, not a rider.
2. **This docblock's opening still claims "every key here has a live read there".** True as written for `style` (the read is in `getMapConfig`) but not on the path this block takes — see 1. Left byte-identical: correcting it is the same card as 1.
